$comment: ForeverLM CloudKit schema v2: the single source of truth (docs/cloudkit-schema-design.md §12.1). Edit this file, then run `node scripts/schema/generate.mjs`; `node scripts/schema/check-generated.mjs` fails while any generated file is stale. Never rename, retype or reuse a key: retired keys go to the type's `reserved` list (§12.6).

stamp.doc: Policy letter, 13-digit epoch milliseconds (server-corrected), 4-digit counter, 8-character device id. Two stamps compare by the 27 characters after the letter, as plain strings (§3.2 rule 3).

recordName.key: the 32 raw bytes of the zone salt (ZoneRoot.salt is their base64)
recordName.doc: recordName = prefix + "_" + base32lower(HMAC-SHA256(zoneSalt, type + "\n" + id))[0..<26] (§3.4). ZoneRoot is always named `root`.

envelope.doc: The payload JSON (§3.2): unknown top-level keys are kept. A string field over spillStringBytes is stored as {"$file": FileRef} under its own stamp (rule 8).

Catalog.doc: Source and Collection metadata, and playlist Entries.

Content.doc: Immutable byte satellites of the private library and every personal satellite; never change-fetched.

Space.doc: One zone per team, family, shared notebook or shared Doc, with a zone-wide CKShare; holds its satellites inline.

policies.L: last writer: the larger stamp wins
policies.S: server first: field-level compare-and-set against the base the writer saw
policies.X: maximum by value; the result carries the larger stamp
policies.N: minimum by value; the result carries the larger stamp
policies.T: text body: an L pointer to a body satellite, plus a three-way text merge when both sides changed since the base

fieldKinds.scalar: any JSON value, merged whole (objects and arrays included)
fieldKinds.map: a JSON object whose keys merge independently; one stamp per key; a removed key has the value null and keeps its stamp
fieldKinds.set: a JSON object of key: true|false; false means removed and is kept so the removal can win against an older add

homeRules.library: always the personal Library (every priv-only type)
homeRules.current: the library the record is written in: privateZone in the personal library, else that space's zone
homeRules.parent: the zone of the record that field names (parents picks the type by kindField): a notebook through resolveNotebook (§4.4), any other parent where this client holds it, first in the library the record is written in; with the parent unknown, where a new record of the parent's type would go. personalIDPrefixes keep a record in Library, and primaryOfSpace puts the record a space of that kind was made for in that space
homeRules.owner: a satellite: the zone of the record that owns it (typeField, field), with privateZone for an owner in the private library; a personal role (roleField) is always in privateZone

jsonTypes.day: calendar day YYYY-MM-DD in the learner's time zone at the time of writing
jsonTypes.id: a logical id of another record (see `ref`)
jsonTypes.workKey: a work key such as doi:10.1038/x (WorkKey.normalize, §4.2)
jsonTypes.deviceID: 8 base32 characters ([a-z2-7]{8}), random per installation; legacy22 is reserved for migrated history (Sitting, ActivityLog) and never drawn
jsonTypes.saltID: 8 lowercase hex characters: the first 8 of sha256 of the zone's 32 salt bytes (§2.4 step 6)
jsonTypes.object: a JSON object with the documented keys

Locator.doc: pdf {page, quads: [[x1,y1,x2,y2,x3,y3,x4,y4]], offset?} with page-normalized 0…1 quads, origin top-left; text {offset, len, quote, prefix, suffix, textHash}; epub {href, cfi, fraction}; media {seconds, end?, duration}; web {fraction}; slide {index, seconds}; doc {bodyHash, start, end, quote}. Unknown kinds and keys are kept.

Span.doc: Lesson item ranges: pages 12–40, 00:10–00:45, one EPUB chapter.

ReaderContext.doc: Provenance of a write; never forks state.

FileRef.doc: A pointer to Content satellites (§3.3). owner = the record that first uploaded the bytes (a copy of the FileRef keeps it, D41); hash = sha256 hex of the decoded bytes; size = decoded bytes; stored = stored bytes; parts = the first 32 hex characters of sha256 of each part's stored bytes, in order, so every satellite name ct:<owner>:<role>:<partHash32> follows from the FileRef; inline = one part held in data; children list dependent satellites so GC never parses bodies; heldBy = the bytes were not uploaded (sync.originals) and live only on that Mac.

SettingValue.doc: Typed JSON (data = base64, date = ms); null = cleared.

Answer.doc: One answer in a Sitting; written once. subject is crd:<id>, qz:<id>#<qid>, src:<id>#walk:<step> or exc:<id>; outcome is graded:<verdict>, remembered, forgot or skipped. Answers that do not count toward scheduling are written too (counted: false).

SpilledString.doc: A string field whose UTF-8 encoding passed spillStringBytes, uploaded as a field.<name> satellite (gzip) and resolved by every reader (§3.2 rule 8).

ArchiveStatus.doc: Source, Collection, Course and Artifact status

IngestState.doc: Source.ingest.state; rank by ord: queued 1, fetching 2, error 3, paywalled 3, ready 4; a paper is ready only with a PDF

LessonItemRole.doc: Entry.role (lesson items); article, podcast, code and other are roles today's course items carry (WP9)

ChatKind.doc: Chat.kind; review, memory, quizSitting, walkthrough and voice are private kinds (D19)

CardStatus.doc: Card.status; the codec never writes a transition out of retired

JobKind.doc: Job.kind: work a Mac does for the iPhone, web or hosted MCP

payload.doc: The envelope (§3.2). Required on every record.

data.doc: An inline satellite body of at most 256 KiB.

asset.doc: One part of a larger satellite body: exactly 48 MiB from native clients, exactly 14 MiB from the web, the last part smaller. Assets are always encrypted at rest; end to end under ADP.

Users.doc: Copied verbatim from cktool export-schema (every container has it).

cloudKit.ignoredOnExportDoc: cloudkit.share exists only after a Dev build saves a CKShare (§2.1 C8); it is never imported, and verify-production.sh leaves it out of the comparison but fails while it is absent, because spaces cannot save a CKShare without it (§12.2, C8).

ZoneRoot.doc: One per zone that holds records: the zone's kind, salt, owner and coordination leases; on the personal root also the cutover's seed, the late-import base and watermark, and the move maps.

salt.doc: Base64 of 32 random bytes: the HMAC key for record names in this zone (and in Catalog and Content for the personal root).

saltID.doc: First 8 hex characters of sha256 of the salt bytes; repeated in every payload of the zone (§2.4 step 6).

minClientRevision.doc: Clients whose schema revision is lower stop sending to this zone and ask for an update (§12.5); starts at 1.

seed.keys: state, startedAt, canaryPassedAt, metadataCompleteAt, completedAt, counts, manifest
seed.doc: Cutover coordination (§13.4), one key per subfield: state (pending|seeding|complete, SeedState), startedAt, canaryPassedAt, metadataCompleteAt, completedAt, counts {records, satellites, bytes} and manifest (a FileRef). Each subfield merges on its own, so a save that writes one (the claim's state, Finish's completedAt and counts, a fold's manifest) never drops another. metadataCompleteAt (set with the canary) lets other Macs reconcile and the web, the hosted MCP and iPhone build N switch while satellites still upload; manifest is a gzip satellite listing every (type, id) the seed uploaded (§13.5). A Mac that holds no library writes state pending; for a brand-new account a Mac, the iPhone or the web that holds none writes an empty complete seed (counts 0, every time set); none of them ever writes seeding, and the hosted MCP writes no root (§2.4).

manifestDeltas.keys: <deviceID>.<passID>: the device and the pass that created the records
manifestDeltas.doc: Personal root only: one gzip list per pass that created records after the seed manifest was written (any Mac's import pass, refresh, deferred catch-up, takeover, P6, reconcile upload; §13.6): the (type, id) it created, or (spaceID, type, id) for a space record. Each pass writes only its own key, so concurrent passes never collide. Every reader takes the manifest and every delta as "was in the new world" (§13.5, §13.6). Past 32 entries the importer folds them and the manifest into a new seed.manifest satellite and clears the folded keys in the same save, so the root stays small.

seedClaim.doc: {device, leaseUntil}: who seeds; a 30-minute lease renewed every 10 minutes by the holder; an expired claim is taken over by a CAS save (§13.4 step 1); never claimed by a Mac that holds no library.

maintenanceLease.doc: {device, leaseUntil}: who runs GC, the orphan janitor, duplicate resolution, moveMaps folding and the practices engine; a 24-hour lease renewed daily. Macs only, and only one that holds the library: the seeder takes it with its claim; any other Mac only after seed.metadataCompleteAt and its own first complete fetch of Library and Catalog. Once the seed is complete, its holder is also the importer (§13.6).

legacyImport.doc: {container, zones, tokens: {<old zone>: base64 change token}, lastOldWriteAt, quietSince, finishedAt, removedAt}: the late-import watermark (§13.6); published with legacyBase in P0 (§13.4) and advanced only by the importer: the seed-claim holder until the seed completes, then the maintenance-lease holder.

legacyBase.keys: shard: 00–3f, the first byte of sha256(old record name) divided by 4, as two hex characters
legacyBase.doc: Personal root only: the shared late-import base (§13.6). Per old record: its change tag, whether it is waiting (a value it gives waits for a record not created yet, §13.6), and for each v2 record the §10 mapping gives it, whether it owns that record (§10, "Who owns what") and a hash of each field, keyed by v2 type, id and field; a body hashes by the content hash its FileRef carries, which for a Doc is the old bodyRevision (§13.6). 64 gzip shards, est. 2–4 MB in all, so every shard stores inline (≈ 30–60 KB each, ≤ 256 KiB; 64 inline shards hold up to 16 MB). Published by the seeder in P0, before its first record (§13.4); advanced only by the importer.

learnerModel.doc: Personal root only: the learner-model satellite in private Content.

archiveIndex.doc: Personal root only: a gzip list of (type, id) per archive zone, rewritten after each archive move batch (§11.4).

moveMaps.doc: Personal root only (D51): one entry per SpaceMoveJob pass (a notebook moved into a space, a Doc moved into its Doc space, a reverse move; a course never moves, §5.5), a gzip list of the (type, id, from zone, to zone) that pass moved. Each is written before the pass deletes its first original and is never rewritten, so two Macs' passes never lose each other's ids. Past 32 entries the maintenance Mac folds them into one folded.<n> entry and clears the folded keys in the same save (§4.4).

familyPlanCode.doc: Family spaces (was the Team payload, schema 137).

sealedMemberKeys.doc: Family member AI keys, each sealed to the member's device key.

primaryID.doc: The notebook or Doc the space was made for.

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

Device.doc: One per installation: platform, build and schema revision for skew gating.

deviceID.doc: Random per installation, [a-z2-7]{8}; the value legacy22 is reserved for migrated history and never drawn (Mac and iOS: a Keychain item that does not sync; web: IndexedDB, written by one elected writer tab per browser; MCP: Durable Object storage).

lastSeenDay.doc: Written on a build change and at most once a week; never on open; read by the compaction gate (§3.2 rule 4) and the schema gate (§12.5).

connectorHealth.doc: connector → {state, lastSeenAt, lastSuccessfulSyncAt}; was the synced connectorHealth.* preferences; lets the web warn about a dead Mac-side feed.

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

Setting.doc: One record per synced setting key: account scope in Library, space scope in a space.

key.doc: A key SyncedPreferenceKeys.isSynced accepts (after the domain prefixes moved out, §10); validated against schema/generated/settings-catalog.json, whose leftOut names the keys only their own writers set (a Notebook Collection's name, notebookCollection.<id>, §3.5.3).

value.doc: Typed JSON; null = cleared (Setting records are never deleted).

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

Source.doc: A work in the library: its identity, metadata and pointers to its content satellites. 1.5–2.5 KB. Nothing member-local: how a source entered a member's library is that member's Mark(provenance).

id.doc: URL sources src_ + hex(sha256("source:v1:" + URLNormalizer.normalize(url))) (SourceIdentity.stableID). A file captured on the iPhone or the web (a scan, photos, a PDF, a shared PDF) gets SourceIdentity.fileID(sha256) = src_ + hex(sha256("source:v1:file:" + <sha256 hex of the bytes>)), so the same bytes captured twice land on one id (D47); the Mac's own file imports keep their path-based ids and gain the file: work key. Every other kind keeps its documented rule (§4.1). The same id in every zone.

primaryKey.doc: The key the id was minted from: url:, doi:, file:, yt:, podcast:, meeting:, x:, gh:, course:, native:.

workKeys.doc: Every identity key known (includes primaryKey); looked up before any mint (§4.2).

type.doc: move_source_type edits it; a skeletal import writes it with a provisional stamp.

typeLocked.doc: The learner set the type by hand (was source_user_state.source_type_manually_set).

title.doc: A skeletal import (iPhone, web, hosted MCP, share sheet) writes it with a provisional stamp (milliseconds 0000000000001), so any real title beats it (§5.4).

url.doc: Canonical URL to open; provisional stamp from a skeletal import.

collectionID.doc: The book, show, channel or meeting series it belongs to.

status.doc: Shared state: in a space it is the team's archive; a copy into a space starts active.

ingest.doc: {ord: [generation, rank], state: queued|fetching|ready|error|paywalled, error?, at, device}: monotonic by ord (rank queued 1, fetching 2, error 3, paywalled 3, ready 4; generation + 1 on a deliberate re-fetch); written by the ingesting device; a paper is ready only with a PDF; a skeletal import writes [0, 1], so it never sends a ready source back to queued.

contentHash.doc: Of the canonical text; versions derived outputs, anchors and highlights.

summary.doc: Abstract or AI summary, at most 1,500 characters; searchable on every device.

metrics.doc: {pageCount?, durationSeconds?, wordCount?, textChars?}; textChars = full canonical length (never truncated).

derived.doc: Machine outputs, each FileRef with gen.

meta.doc: paper {pmid, pmcid, arxivID, pdfStatus, paywallCheckedAt, journal, publisher, citationCount}; podcast {feedURL, guid, audioURL, episodeNumber, showName}; video {youtubeID, channelID, channelName} (a like is the member's Mark(liked)); meeting {startAt, endAt, platform, zoomID, participants, groupKey, attachments: {key: {kind, title, url, fileRole?}}}; book {isbn, bookID, chapterIndex, chapterPath, pageStart, pageCount: a chapter of a book kept as one file is the pages pageStart (0-based) ..< pageStart + pageCount of the book's PDF, which its files.pdf names (owner = the book's Collection id, the same FileRef on every chapter)}; xPost {postID, handle}; repo {owner, name, branch}; course {provider, externalURL}; article {siteName, archivedAt}.

copiedFrom.doc: {zone: personal|<spaceID>, at, by: Person}: space copies only.

mergedInto.doc: Duplicate resolution: a permanent redirect; the first acknowledged resolution stands; resolveSource() follows it (§4.2).

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change; never moved by opening, filing or sync.

reservedDoc.signature: Per-source portable vector (D27); deferred, not written in R1.

Collection.doc: A book, podcast show, YouTube channel, playlist or meeting series. Members point at it with Source.collectionID; playlist members are Entries. Following it is per member: Mark(following); a space refreshes it only through the space Setting follow.<collectionID>.

externalKey.doc: ISBN or book key, feed URL, channel id, playlist id, meeting group key.

feed.doc: {feedURL?, channelID?, playlistID?}: what can be followed (a shared fact).

status.doc: meetings.removedGroupIdentities, userCourseNames and userMeetingGroupNames stay Settings in R1.

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

Notebook.doc: A notebook. Notes live in its Notes Doc (Artifact notes:<id>); membership, ticks and order are not in this record. A merged or moved notebook stays for ever as a stub (status merged or moved); a late edit to one of its other fields is forwarded once, through the fold to a merge's survivor or verbatim to the space copy (§5.2).

id.doc: Some existing ids are uppercase UUIDs; ids compare exactly.

title.doc: A leading emoji is the icon, unless files.cover is set (D53).

researchQuestions.doc: qid → {text, status: open|answered|dropped, orderKey, createdAt}; per-question merge (was a JSON array).

openQuestions.doc: gid → {text, status: open|resolved, createdAt, sourceIDs?} (was learning_goal_gaps).

boardLists.doc: lid → {title, orderKey, createdAt}: the lists a learner added to the notebook's task Board, drawn between In progress and Done in orderKey order; per-list merge. A Task names one in listID.

relatedNotebookIDs.doc: The notebooks this one may draw on in its chats ("Uses context from"; shared). Being listed feeds no context: each member ticks listed notebooks into their own chats' context in NotebookState.contextNotebooks, and the Studio never reads them (D52, §5.6).

homeArtifactID.doc: The notebook's own linked Doc (was learning_goals.artifact_id).

files.doc: The AI-drawn cover (D53), shown in place of the leading-emoji icon; its gen names model and prompt. Written from WP31 on (after R1); R1 clients keep it and show the emoji.

layout.doc: What the Sources column shows for everyone (default sources); course opens it on the page of a course the notebook follows (§8d).

primaryCourseID.doc: The followed course course mode shows by default; ignored unless the notebook has an active follow Entry for it (§8d).

mergedInto.doc: Permanent redirect after a merge, or after an emptying split, which points the parent at its heir (§5.2, D48). The first acknowledged fold stands; a fold whose write loses keeps what it already moved, and the learner is told.

foldKind.doc: Written in the same save as mergedInto: merge when the stub was merged away (its exclusions are ignored, and each member's devices union its context-notebook ticks and collections into the survivor's), split when an emptying split left it (each member's devices hand its exclusions, ticks and collections to the heir), §5.2.

movingTo.doc: A spaceID, set on the original while it moves into a space (§5.3); other devices hide the original and put new children into the space once their replica holds the notebook's copy there, else into Library, where the move's catch-up copies them (§4.4); resolveNotebook() does not follow it.

movedTo.doc: A spaceID, on the Library stub a move into a space leaves behind (§5.3); permanent; resolveNotebook() follows it into the space. The ids the move copied are listed in ZoneRoot.moveMaps (D51), not on the stub.

copiedFrom.doc: {zone, notebookID, at, by: Person}: a copy into someone else's space.

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change; the recently-edited sort key.

Goal.doc: A personal plan toward a date. Its sources are Entries with containerKind goal.

notebookID.doc: The notebook it serves (may be a space notebook).

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

Entry.doc: The ordered edge: an item in a notebook, goal, lesson or playlist. The same item added to the same container on two devices gets the same record name. An Entry whose item is missing is kept and hidden on read; twin and merged Entries copy state and approval values and stamps verbatim (§5.6).
Entry.zoneRule: Catalog holds playlist Entries only; notebook, goal and lesson Entries are in Library or the container's space.

id.doc: A second span of the same source in one lesson takes #2, then #3; the first has no suffix.

containerID.doc: The back-pointer every merge, split and delete re-points.

itemID.doc: A notebook's Entry of itemKind course is its follow of that course, the one tie between the two (§5.5). In the same library (the private library = Library + Catalog + Content; a space = its zone); the items of personal containers (Goal) resolve by wire id across the personal library and every space.

state.doc: Remove and re-add flip this field; Entries are never deleted while their container is live (active or archived); the Entries of a merged notebook, or of the parent of an emptying split, are deleted by the job once their twins exist (§5.2).

approval.doc: Notebook containers; absent = approved. Shared editorial state that travels in spaces; rejected stops discovery from proposing the item again.

orderKey.doc: Study order, lesson order, playlist order.

span.doc: The part of the source a lesson item covers (replaces source_units, 0 rows).

required.doc: Lesson items: counts toward completion (default true).

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

Course.doc: A course and its gate policy. A course lives in no notebook (2026-10-03): it is in the personal Library, or in a space as that space's own; a notebook only follows it, by an Entry of itemKind course (§5.5). The Courses tab's order is the account Setting studio.courseOrder.

meta.doc: courseCode (string, was courses.course_code) and instructors (array of strings, was courses.instructors), which list_courses and get_course print.

policy.doc: {gateQuizzes: bool, pass: {right: int, of: int} | null}; a null pass = rightNeededToPass(total) = ceil(3·total/4) (LectureQuizScore).

createdAt.doc: The record now carries a created date (the web used to guess it).

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

reservedDoc.notebookID: Retired in revision 9: the course's home notebook. A course lives in no notebook; a notebook follows a course by an Entry of itemKind course. Reserved once no client named it (COURSE9).
reservedDoc.homing: Retired in revision 9: whether the learner had confirmed the course's home notebook. A course lives in no notebook.

Lesson.doc: A lesson in a course, in the course's zone. Its items are Entries with containerKind lesson.

objectives.doc: "You should be able to say…"; feeds the quiz writer and the card drafter.

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

Quiz.doc: A course quiz in the course's zone, placed on the path by lessonID: after that lesson, and among the quizzes after one lesson by kind, then title (no quiz Entry, as built by WP9).

id.doc: New quizzes keep the cq- ids the Mac mints (CourseQuizPlanning in CourseCore.swift: a digest of the course and its lectures).

lessonID.doc: The lesson it follows on the path (was course_quizzes.after_lecture_id).

revision.doc: +1 on every change to the questions; sittings record it ("previous version" scores).

questions.doc: gzip JSON [{id, kind, prompt, choices?, answer, rubric?, explanation?, pictureKey?}] (was 381 KB inline over 25 quizzes).

pictures.doc: One satellite per picture (was a 64 MB bundle and 114 KB of inline artwork).

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

Enrollment.doc: A learner's own enrollment in a course. Created only by an explicit act (Enroll, set focus, set pace), never by opening a course.

focus.doc: What the learner wants from the course, in their words (was course.focus.<courseID>).

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

Chat.doc: A chat or review session. Only kinds chat and transcript may live in a space; the private kinds stay in the member's Library even when filed in a space notebook (D19). Which sources' text a chat loaded stays local to each Mac; the number of exchanges is counted on read.

kind.doc: review, memory, quizSitting, walkthrough and voice are private kinds (D19). Chats recorded before the kind existed get theirs from ChatKindClassifier (D50, §10); new chats are written with their kind by their creation site. voice is legacy only: since 76d92fe83 a spoken conversation is saved as the chat or review it drives.

notebookID.doc: Its home (may name a space notebook from the private Library).

subject.doc: What it is about (a source, Doc, quiz).

contextMode.doc: notebook = the notebook's chat context for the member reading it (§5.6, D52): its own active approved entries and those of the listed notebooks the member ticked into context, minus the member's exclusions.

docLinks.doc: linkID → {artifactID, anchorRevision, start, end, quote, sectionTitle, createdAt}: Doc passages the chat was opened on (was artifact_chat_links nested in the session).

briefing.doc: Private kinds; up to 803 KB today.

marksReviewed.doc: Whether an import_review_chat call with session_id and no mark_reviewed counts the sources it adds as reviewed (today's appendMarksReviewed default, MCPTools+ReviewSessions.swift). Set at creation from mark_reviewed by the Mac and the gateway; a later explicit mark_reviewed: false writes false; derived at activation by today's rule, kind IS NULL OR kind = 'review'; absent = true only for kind review.

overallScore.doc: Private kinds only (privateKindsOnly): SpaceWriteGuard refuses it in a space (§9.2).

editedAt.doc: Time of the last exchange; max, so two devices appending never fight.

Exchange.doc: One complete turn of a chat, in the chat's zone. Sent once complete; every field is S (the first acknowledged value stands); a regeneration is a new Exchange with supersedes. Any string over 32 KiB is spilled (§3.2 rule 8). Thumbs ratings are Mark(kind rated), never on the Exchange.

id.doc: Turns a continued chat appended on the iPhone keep their ids (<session>::continued::<sitting>::<nnnn>); with one record per Exchange nothing merges them.

seq.doc: 1 + the highest seq the writer has seen; display order is (seq, createdAt, id), so two devices appending at once both survive.

question.doc: The opening turn: the learner's message in a chat, the tutor's question in a review.

userAnswer.doc: The learner's answer in a review.

evaluation.doc: The reply or the tutor's evaluation (spilled above 32 KiB, §3.2 rule 8).

score.doc: Private chat kinds only (privateKindsOnly); SpaceWriteGuard refuses it in a space, as it refuses grading.

citedSourceIDs.doc: What the reply cited (discussed versus attached, for memory).

contextText.doc: The passage text sent with the message (was context_content).

contextAnchor.doc: {target: ItemRef, locator: Locator, quote}: the same passage, anchored, so the Reader can list chats about this passage.

attachments.doc: [{role: picture|file, file: FileRef}]: generated chat pictures now sync.

grading.doc: {ideaCoverage: [{ideaID, status}], questionVerdict, operation, steer}: private chat kinds only (privateKindsOnly); SpaceWriteGuard refuses it in a space.

Artifact.doc: A Doc, Notes Doc, Site, animation, audio overview, report, file, picture, linked page, skill, explainer or lesson.

id.doc: The five special forms are deterministic: a Notes Doc notes:<notebookID>; a member's draft of a space Doc draft:<spaceArtifactID>; a project file file:<notebookID>:<sha256hex(path)>; a standalone generated picture picture:<image id> (the id GeneratedImageReference uses); and a "Recovered:" Doc recovered:<artifactID>:<hash>, hash being the content hash of the body it saves (§6.2, §13.6), so every pass that meets the same lost body makes the same one record.

notebookID.doc: Home notebook (cross-zone allowed for the owner).

linkedNotebookIDs.doc: Other notebooks it is filed in (was global_artifact_project_links).

body.doc: The body satellite: Markdown package, site bundle, animation package, audio, file bytes. Published on idle (≥ 30 s), on close, on Publish and before a send that needs it, never per keystroke (D44).

files.doc: Pictures and media used by the body.

path.doc: file kind: path in the notebook's workspace folder (was project_files).

publish.doc: {kind: doc|site, slug, url, publishedHash, publishedAt, publishedBy: Person, protected: bool}: R2 publishing state.

draftOf.doc: {spaceID, artifactID, baseHash}: a member's private draft of a space Doc.

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

Comment.doc: A comment on a Doc, in the artifact's zone.

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

Highlight.doc: A learner's highlight, keyed on the canonical source id so it shows on the personal copy and every space copy. Survives the source's deletion.

locator.doc: PDF quads and/or a text quote.

contentHash.doc: The text version it was made on; drives re-anchoring.

context.doc: Where it was made (notebook, lesson, chat).

editedAt.doc: Ms of the last content change.

ReadingState.doc: One record per person per work, the same whether the source is opened from the library, a notebook, a lesson or a team copy. Created only when the position or a flag first changes.

furthest.doc: [epoch, fraction]: furthest progress 0…1; mark unread writes [epoch+1, 0] so a reset beats older maxima.

completedAt.doc: Completed (carries the 57 notebook-item completions, §10); null = not completed.

consumedAt.doc: Listened or watched to the end (was source_user_state.is_consumed); null = not consumed.

listen.doc: {globalTime, appleCharacterOffset?, contentSignature?, at}: the text-to-speech resume point, today's ArticleSpeechPlaybackPosition whole (seconds into the narration, the character offset Apple's voices resume from, the signature of the text it was made on). Was listen.position.* and the playback-position.json beside each narration in iCloud Drive; the newer updatedAt wins, as today (§13.3 step 3c).

walk.keys: walkthrough variant: main (the source's or the animation's own walk) or course.<courseID>

params.doc: A JSON object of at most 16 KiB. ingestURL: {url, workKeys, target?}; ingestFile: {file: FileRef, sha256, title?, capture: scan|photos|pdf|share, target?}, written only after the file's pdf satellites are acknowledged; target = {notebookID | goalID, approval} names where the claiming Mac files the source (§5.4, D47). moveToSpace (the Job's target is nb:<id>): {spaceID} for a space the learner owns, or {newSpace: {kind, name}} (§5.3).

claim.doc: {device, at}: the first acknowledged claim wins (CAS); a Mac starts the job only after its claim is acknowledged; an expired lease may be taken over by a CAS save.

expiresAt.doc: requestedAt + 7 days; the maintenance Mac deletes a Job past it only once it is done, failed or cancelled: a queued Job that no Mac has claimed never expires, so a capture waits for a Mac however long it lags.

Content.doc: An immutable byte satellite named by owner, role and the hash of its stored bytes; fetched by name, never change-fetched. A create collision counts as success only after the stored part fields (partHash, partBytes, enc) match; hash, size, part and parts describe the file of whoever uploaded the part first (§3.5.30 rule 1).
Content.zoneRule: Content for private owners and every personal satellite; the owner's space for space owners.

id.doc: partHash32 = the first 32 hex characters of sha256 of that part's stored bytes (after gzip when enc = gzip); the FileRef lists every part's hash, so every name follows from it.

ownerType.doc: The record type of the owner.

hash.doc: sha256 of the whole decoded file (all parts reassembled and decoded) as the part's first uploader had it; a later file that shares the part may differ, so a collision never compares it.

size.doc: Decoded bytes of the whole content.

parts.doc: ≥ 1; parts are exactly 48 MiB (native) or 14 MiB (web), the last smaller.

partHash.doc: sha256 of this part's stored bytes; its first 32 hex characters are in the name.

sync.originals.doc: Which original files the library uploads (D38): all (the default), none over 50 MB, or none; a file kept back is held by a named Mac (FileRef.heldBy).

aiTask..doc: Retired: a task's custom prompt, in place of the built-in one (KeychainService.taskPrompt). No control or tool sets one any more (setTaskPrompt has no caller); a value an older build wrote is still read.
Retired 2026-09-28 (a task's own model is aiRoute.task.<task> since 2026-10-07; the chat's picks are per session).

aiRoute.task..doc: A Background task's model of its own, which wins over Background's (KeychainService.ownRoute, Settings › Background › Tasks): the AIModelRoutePreference JSON {version, provider, model}. Retired 2026-09-28 and back since 2026-10-07; absent, the task follows Background's Text-only or Multimodal model. Canvas Voice is given one the first time the learner speaks to a canvas (KeychainService.seedCanvasVoiceRoute, marked by aiSeeded.task.canvas_voice), and Card Answer Check the first time a card is checked (seedCardAnswerCheckRoute, aiSeeded.task.card_answer_check), and Go Deeper the first time it is pressed (seedGoDeeperRoute, aiSeeded.task.card_go_deeper).

aiHost..doc: Which OpenRouter host serves one model in one slot: OpenRouterHostPreference as JSON text; model is the lowercased slug.

aiBackups..doc: The models a slot falls back to, in order: a JSON array of {provider, model}, at most AIBackupModels.limit (10).

aiBackground..doc: Background's text provider, kept current for older builds beside aiRoute.background.
Background's text model for that provider (its AIProvider raw value), kept current beside aiRoute.background.
The learner agreed to background AI usage in Getting Started.
Meeting tasks may run on a free Background model (MeetingModels.mayUseFreeKey).
Retired: the unsuffixed Background model, replaced by aiBackground.model.<provider>.
Retired with the direct Meta trial (KeychainService.purgeRetiredProviderData).
Retired with the direct Meta trial: its start (epoch seconds) and its limit in dollars.

readAloud.modelVoice..doc: The voice a text-to-speech model was last given (ArticleSpeechVoiceMemory): choosing the model again brings it back. The selected voice itself is macos.tts.openrouter.voice.

readAloud.voiceRating..doc: The learner's thumbs on one model's voice (ArticleSpeechVoiceRating); absent is no rating.

memory.reviewDepth.type..doc: How much of a memory review a kind of source gets by default (MemoryReviewDepth); sourceType is lowercased.

notebook.thinkFirst..doc: One notebook's Think first level, the learner's own (account scope, so a teammate's choice never changes it), over thinkFirst.level; absent means the library's level applies. A Setting rather than a NotebookState field, like notebook.naming., so no store schema changes.

follow..doc: A space's explicit refresh of a followed Collection: {autoImport, runnerDeviceID}, naming the one member's Mac that imports the feed (§3.5.5). The Mac writes it through SpaceFollows, not as a synced preference: the catalog's origin spec only says no preference key carries it.

map.layout..doc: One of the learner's canvases (docs/knowledge-map-design.md, "Canvases in the Space"), as a JSON string {version, placements, regions, edges, removed, name, created, trash} (KnowledgeMapLayout): each placed card's spot, each region the learner drew and each arrow, every entry stamped with the time it was written and every removal kept as a tombstone, so two copies merge entry by entry; and the canvas itself, its name and Trash mark stamped the same way and the second it was made. One row per canvas, and every row is a canvas listed in the Space: mapID is library for the first canvas, else cnv- and a lowercase UUID. Written by the Canvas pane, the Space and MCP's canvas tools on the Mac, never set_app_setting: a lens a chat asks for changes nothing until the learner keeps it.

aiSeeded.task..doc: That ForeverLM gave the task its starting model of its own, once for the account (true); absent until then. Written only by KeychainService.seedCanvasVoiceRoute, seedCardAnswerCheckRoute and seedGoDeeperRoute, so a learner who sends Canvas Voice, Card Answer Check or Go Deeper back to Background's model is not given the starting model again, on this Mac or another; never set_app_setting.

notebook.naming..doc: The name and card description ForeverLM last put on a notebook made without a name, as a JSON string {title, summary?, sources?, exchanges?} (NotebookNaming.Mark): ForeverLM may rename the notebook only while its title and summary are still these. Absent means ForeverLM leaves the name alone; every learner edit of the title or description removes it. Written by the notebook creators and the naming step (Mac, iPhone, MCP create_project without a title), never set_app_setting.

studio.workspaceView..doc: One saved workspace view per row (StudioSavedWorkspaceView), so monitor arrangements never contend: the window arrangement the learner saved with Save Workspace View, as the window's own stored form. Written by the window that saves or deletes it, never set_app_setting: a chat has no window to arrange.

notebook.questions..doc: The questions a notebook's guide suggested for its sources, and which were asked, as a JSON string {sources, questions, asked} (NotebookSuggestedQuestions.Kept): sources is the fingerprint of the notebook's source ids the questions were suggested for; the guide offers the questions not asked yet in every new chat without a model call, and offers Suggest questions again only when the fingerprint changes. Per member, one row per notebook. Written by the Mac's notebook chat when an answer suggests questions or one is asked, never set_app_setting.

notebookCollection..doc: A Notebook Collection's name (a leading emoji is its icon), one Setting per collection, null once the collection is deleted. Written by the collection writers (the Notebooks home on each client, MCP update_notebook_collection on the Mac), never set_app_setting (§3.5.3).

pageSpace..doc: The name of one of the learner's spaces of pages (PageSpaces; ChatGPT's spaces, the Space sidebar's Spaces), a leading emoji its icon; spaceID is psp- and a lowercase UUID. One Setting per space, null once the space is deleted. The learner's own grouping, not a sync space (D4): written by the Space sidebar on the Mac and the web and by MCP update_space on the Mac, never set_app_setting.

pageSpaceTrash..doc: When one of the learner's spaces of pages (pageSpace.<spaceID>) went to Trash, as whole seconds since 1970 in text; absent while the space is in use (PageSpaces; Codex's Space Trash holds spaces as well as pages). A space in Trash leaves the sidebar and lists no pages, its pages stay in All and keep their page.space rows, so Restore brings the space back as it was; Delete Forever removes the name, the page rows and this row. A row whose pageSpace name is gone is read past. Written by the Space on the Mac and the web, never set_app_setting.

page.space..doc: The one space of pages (pageSpace.<spaceID>) a page, linked Google Doc, site or reading is in, as its spaceID; absent when it is in none. One Setting per record, per member, never a field of the Doc: an id whose pageSpace name is gone (deleted, or not arrived yet) is read past, and deleting a space removes the rows naming it that the deleting device holds. Written by Move to Space and New page in a space on the Mac and the web, and by MCP update_space on the Mac, never set_app_setting.

page.pinned..doc: When the learner pinned a page, a linked Google Doc or a site (PagePins; ChatGPT's Pin, the Space sidebar's Pinned section), as the whole seconds since 1970 in text; absent when it is not pinned, and the newest pin lists first. One Setting per record, per member, never a field of the Doc: only the learner's own pages pin, never a team's. Written by Pin and Unpin on the Mac and the web, never set_app_setting.

chat.pinned..doc: When the learner pinned a chat, or the place a drag gave it (ChatPins; Codex's Pin chat, Home's Pinned section), as whole seconds since 1970 in text; absent when it is not pinned, and the highest lists first. One Setting per chat, per member, never a field of the Chat; a day's memory review never pins. Written by Pin Chat, Unpin Chat and a drag in Pinned on the Mac and the web, and by MCP update_review_session is_pinned on the Mac, never set_app_setting.

page.parent..doc: The page a page is nested under (PageParents; ChatGPT's subpages, the Space lists' nested rows), as the parent's Artifact id; absent when the page is top-level. One Setting per child, per member, never a field of the Doc: only the learner's own Markdown pages nest, under another of their own, never a team's. An id that names a page that is gone, in Trash or not the learner's own is read past (its children list at the top and the row stays, so restoring the parent brings them back), and a cycle two devices made at once is cut at its smallest id. Written by Move to Page, New Subpage, Remove from Parent and the editor's Page row on the Mac, never set_app_setting.

spaceList..doc: One of the learner's lists in the Space (SpaceLists; ChatGPT's To-do list among the pages): a list of goals or of ideas, as a JSON string {kind: goals|ideas, name, created, at, trashed} in seconds since 1970, trashed absent while it is in use; listID is lst- and a lowercase UUID. One Setting per list, the newer write winning whole, null once deleted forever. The learner's own grouping: the goals and ideas stay records of their own. Written by the Space on the Mac and by MCP's list tools there, never set_app_setting.

spaceListItem..doc: The one list in the Space (spaceList.<listID>) a goal or an idea is in, as its listID; absent when it is in none. One Setting per record, per member, never a field of the goal or idea: an id whose list row is gone is read past, and deleting a list removes the rows naming it that the deleting device holds. Written by the Space on the Mac and by MCP's list tools there, never set_app_setting.

reader.pdfRotations..doc: The pages of one PDF source the learner turned in the reader, as a JSON string {"<page>": <degrees>}: a zero-based page of the source (a chapter of a book counts from its own first page; a page before the first chapter is negative), clockwise degrees in 90, 180 or 270 added to the page's own rotation in the file, a page turned full circle left out. One Setting per source, per member, never a field of the Source: the library file is shared and never rewritten for a reading preference, and a team's copy of the source carries no member's turns. Written by Rotate Page in the Mac reader, never set_app_setting; the iPhone and the web do not read it yet.

images.notebookCoverBackfill..doc: The cover backfill's claim and completion marker for one zone (D53, §5.9): {state: running|done, by: deviceID, at}, in Library, a space's in its owner's Library. No synced preference: only the backfill on the maintenance Mac writes it, by a compare-and-set save beside the engine, never through user_preferences; set_app_setting on the Mac and in the hosted MCP refuses it, and the web and the iPhone never write it.
